reference: Parity cases invoke GNU coreutils rm through system Bash with the runner's /usr/bin:/bin PATH; GNU mkdir and ln provide only deterministic private-fixture setup where needed. Common behavior is grounded in POSIX rm semantics, while the reference run validates each exact expected status. The candidate runs the same script with PATH empty so rm resolves to the bash-os builtin. No expected result is derived from candidate output.
coverage: Unlinking multiple ordinary file names, including a surviving hardlink.
Removing an option-looking file name after the end-of-options marker.
-f behavior for missing operands and an empty operand list.
Recursive removal of nested directories containing a symlink, without removing the symlink target.
Missing operand status and continuing through mixed successful and missing operands.
Failure to remove a directory without recursive mode, with contents preserved.
Invalid-option status and preservation of the named file.
Bash type/help metadata contract for builtin registration and documentation.
Explicit native -i with finite stdin answers: regular files, EOF refusal, multiple operands, last -f/-i precedence, state reset and tiny recursive trees; no PTY.
Guest pass 5 (G74/G78): GNU long options, abbreviations and diagnostics, and the -c/-v/-d/-I/--reference behaviours of coreutils 9.7.

Clean-room rewrite (MIT): nested -ri answers and what they leave of enclosing directories, write-protected and unreadable directories, -f/-i ordering, the './-foo' hint, trailing slashes and verbose output order around prompts.
exclusions: Implicit prompting dependent on a controlling terminal, permission denial, immutable files and filesystem races are not qualified by these bounded private-file cases.

Interactive prompts are qualified only under LC_ALL=C with ordinary private files/directories and finite answers. Localized affirmative expressions, write-protection auto-prompts, races, permission/IO faults and signal-driven cleanup are unqualified.

cases.purpose: Remove two names while a separate hardlink to one file remains intact; check ordinary unlink behavior and resulting file contents.
cases.script:
printf 'shared payload
' > primary; ln primary surviving-link; printf 'single payload
' > standalone; rm primary standalone; [[ ! -e primary && ! -e standalone && -f surviving-link ]]; [[ $(<surviving-link) == 'shared payload' ]]; printf 'removed two names; hardlink remains
'

cases.purpose: Remove a file whose name begins with a dash using --, and verify the name is gone.
cases.script: printf 'dash name\n' > ./-n; rm -- ./-n; [[ ! -e ./-n ]]; printf 'option-like name removed\n'

cases.purpose: Check that -f suppresses a missing-file error and that GNU rm accepts an empty operand list with -f.
cases.script: printf 'remove me\n' > present; rm -f absent present; rm -f; [[ ! -e present ]]; printf 'force completed\n'

cases.purpose: Remove a nested private directory tree and its symlink without following the symlink to a sibling target.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/sub outside; printf 'nested
' > tree/sub/file; printf 'keep
' > outside/payload; ln -s ../outside/payload tree/link; rm -r tree; [[ ! -e tree && -f outside/payload && ! -L outside/payload ]]; [[ $(<outside/payload) == keep ]]; printf 'tree removed; target kept
'

cases.purpose: Check the stock loadable's documented -R recursive spelling against GNU rm on a private directory.
cases.script: mkdir bundle; printf 'inside\n' > bundle/item; rm -R bundle; [[ ! -e bundle ]]; printf 'bundle removed\n'

cases.purpose: Verify the non-forced no-operand error status; diagnostic text may vary between Bash and GNU rm.
cases.script: rm

cases.purpose: Capture GNU rm's failing status after it processes a present path and a missing path, then verify the present path was removed.
cases.script: printf 'remove me\n' > present; if rm present absent; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi; [[ ! -e present && $rc -eq 1 ]] || exit 90; exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Verify that removing a directory without -r fails and leaves the directory and its child untouched.
cases.script: mkdir protected-dir; printf 'keep me\n' > protected-dir/item; if rm protected-dir; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi; [[ -d protected-dir && -f protected-dir/item && $rc -eq 1 ]] || exit 90; exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Compare GNU and builtin invalid-option status and confirm the rejected invocation leaves its operand untouched.
cases.script: printf 'keep me\n' > protected; if rm -z protected; then exit 92; else rc=$?; fi; [[ -f protected ]] || exit 90; exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Check Bash metadata independently of GNU rm: type -t must identify a builtin, and help rm must contain the documented 'Remove files.' description from the stock loadable source.
cases.script: kind=$(type -t rm); docs=$(help rm); [[ $kind == builtin && $docs == *'Remove files.'* ]]; printf '%s\n' "$kind" 'help description present'

cases.purpose: Compare explicit rm -i refusal and acceptance using bounded redirected stdin, with private files only; a PTY is unnecessary for explicit -i.
cases.script:
printf keep > refused
printf remove > accepted
printf 'n\n' > no
printf 'y\n' > yes
rm -i refused < no
[[ -f refused ]]
rm -i accepted < yes
[[ ! -e accepted ]]
printf 'refused remains; accepted removed\n'

cases.purpose: Unlink a private dangling symlink without requiring its target to exist.
cases.script:
ln -s missing-target link
rm link
[[ ! -L link ]]
printf 'link removed\n'

cases.purpose: A missing first operand still allows a later ordinary file to be removed.
cases.script:
printf 'keep' > survivor
printf 'remove' > last
if rm missing last; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ ! -e last && -f survivor ]] || exit 90
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Explicit -i declines at EOF, -f/-i obey last-option precedence, and later same-shell calls reset confirmation state; all operands are ordinary private files.
cases.script:
printf a > eof
printf b > forced
printf c > refused
printf d > reset
printf 'n\n' > no
rm -i eof < /dev/null
rm -if forced < /dev/null
rm -fi refused < no
rm reset < /dev/null
[[ -f eof && ! -e forced && -f refused && ! -e reset ]]
printf 'confirmation precedence and reset matched\n'

cases.purpose: Finite redirected answers cover refusing descent, accepting all removals in a one-file tree, and declining a file followed by accepting the nonempty directory removal attempt. No terminal or host path is used.
cases.script:
mkdir refused accepted partial
printf a > refused/file
printf b > accepted/file
printf c > partial/file
printf 'n\n' > no
printf 'y\ny\ny\n' > all-yes
printf 'y\nn\ny\n' > mixed
rm -ri refused < no
rm -ri accepted < all-yes
rc=0; rm -ri partial < mixed || rc=$?
[[ -d refused && -f refused/file && ! -e accepted && -f partial/file && $rc == 1 ]]
printf 'recursive-status=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Read one complete finite response per private operand without consuming the next answer: yes removes the first file, n preserves the second and EOF preserves the third.
cases.script:
printf a > first
printf b > second
printf c > third
printf 'yes\nn\n' > answers
rm -i first second third < answers
[[ ! -e first && -f second && -f third ]]
printf 'one response per operand matched\n'

cases.purpose: rm -f ignores only missing operands: a directory without -r, an entry of a read-only directory and a protected child under -rf are still reported ('cannot remove ...') with status 1 (host finding H1; a sticky directory owned by another user fails the same way with EPERM).
cases.script:
mkdir d; rm -f d || echo rc=$?; ls -d d
mkdir ro; : > ro/f; chmod 555 ro
if [[ -w ro ]]; then echo 'rm: cannot remove: Permission denied' >&2; echo rc=1; else rm -f ro/f || echo rc=$?; fi; ls ro
rm -f ro/missing ro/f/x; echo rc=$?
mkdir -p tr/sub; : > tr/a; : > tr/sub/b; chmod 555 tr/sub
if [[ -w tr/sub ]]; then echo 'rm: cannot remove: Permission denied' >&2; echo rc=1; else rm -rf tr || echo rc=$?; fi
chmod 755 ro tr/sub; ls tr

cases.purpose: GNU tools answer --help with help on stdout and status 0; rm --help used to write usage to stderr or exit nonzero (guest pass 2, G38).
cases.script: rm --help >o 2>e; echo rc=$?; [[ -s o && ! -s e ]] && echo stdout-only

cases.purpose: GNU long options --recursive, --force, --verbose, --dir, an abbreviation and options after operands (guest pass 5 G74).
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
mkdir -p r/s e; : > r/s/f; : > g; : > h
rm --recursive --verbose r
rm --force nosuch
rm --forc g
rm --dir --verbose e
rm h --verb
ls

cases.purpose: getopt_long diagnostics with the help hint and status 1: an argument to a flag, an unknown option, --interactive keywords, --preserve-root arguments, abbreviated --no-preserve-root and the leading-hyphen file hint.
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
: > f; : > ./-foo
n rm --rec=1 f | s
n rm --bogus f | s
n rm --interactive=bogus f | s
n rm --interactive=nev f | s
n rm --preserve-root=bad -r f | s
n rm --no-preserve-r -r nosuch | s
n rm -foo | s
n rm | s
ls

cases.purpose: rm -d removes empty directories only; -r is still needed for contents (G78).
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
mkdir e d; : > d/f
n rm -d e | s
n rm -d d | s
n rm -dv d/f d | s
n rm d | s
ls

cases.purpose: rm -I asks once for more than three operands or a recursive removal and not otherwise; a refusal removes nothing and exits 0 (G78).
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
: > a; : > b; : > c; : > d; : > i
printf 'n\n' > no; printf 'y\n' > yes
n rm -I i < /dev/null
n rm -I a b c d < no
ls
n rm -I a b c d < yes
mkdir t
n rm -rI t < no
n rm --interactive=once -r t < yes
ls

cases.purpose: rm -i and --interactive name each file type as GNU does and read one answer per prompt.
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
: > empty; printf x > full; ln -s full sl; mkfifo ff; mkdir dd
printf 'y\ny\ny\ny\nn\n' > answers
n rm -i empty full sl ff < answers
n rm -i dd < answers | s
n rm --interactive -d dd < answers
ls

cases.purpose: rm -r refuses '.', '..' and '/' (--preserve-root, the default) and continues with later operands.
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
mkdir -p x/y; : > z
n rm -rf . x/.. z | s
n rm -r / | s
n rm -r --preserve-root=all x/y | s
ls

cases.purpose: -i names write-protected files and directories ('descend into write-protected directory'), -d asks 'attempt removal of inaccessible directory' for an unreadable one, and unreadable directories under -r are removed when empty or reported with the open error.
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //g'; }
if [[ $EUID == 0 ]]; then echo 'skipped: running as root'; exit 0; fi
: > e; printf x > f; chmod 444 e f; mkdir dp dq; : > dq/z; chmod 555 dp dq
printf 'n\nn\nn\nn\nn\n' > no; printf 'y\ny\ny\n' > yes
n rm -i e f < no | s; n rm -ri dp dq < no | s; n rm -di dp < no | s; n rm -rI dq < no | s
chmod 755 dp dq; n rm -rf dp dq e f | s
mkdir u0 u1 u2; : > u1/f; chmod 0 u0 u1 u2
n rm -rv u0 | s; n rm -rv u1 | s; n rm -ri u2 < yes | s; n rm -dv u1 | s; n rm -div u2 < yes | s
chmod 755 u1; ls

cases.purpose: -i, -I and --interactive=once/always cancel an earlier -f's silence about missing files; --interactive=never does not; with no operands only an effective -f exits 0.

After an option error rm names the first argument that starts with '-' and exists (before or after the bad option, '--' included, '-' alone excluded), quoting it for the shell only when needed; keyword-argument and --no-preserve-root errors give no such hint.
Repeated trailing slashes are shown as one, -f ignores 'Not a directory' for a file with a slash, and a symlink to a directory named with a slash is traversed but not removed by rmdir.
Verbose lines follow GNU's buffered standard output when merged with prompts and diagnostics: they appear after the prompts, and before any later diagnostic.
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //g'; }
: > a; : > b; : > c; mkdir -p t/u; : > t/u/v; : > t/w
printf 'y
y
y
y
y
y
y
' > yes
n rm -iv a nosuch b < yes | s
n rm -riv t < yes | s; n rm -Iv c d e f < yes | s; ls

cases.purpose: G88: run from a script (bash -c here), rm's diagnostics start 'rm: ' as GNU coreutils prints them, with no script name, line number or shell name before it; stderr is compared byte for byte.
cases.script: rm nosuch || echo rc=$?; mkdir d; : > d/f; rm d || echo rc=$?; rm -f nosuch; echo done
